questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Who tries to stop the servants fighting in Act 1 Scene 1?
questions.why: Benvolio draws his sword to part the brawling servants, showing his peacemaking role, before Tybalt escalates it — Tybalt actually fuels the fight, he doesn't stop it.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In C–Am–F–G, which chord provides the most tension, wanting to resolve back to C?
questions.why: G is the 'V' chord, the dominant, which creates tension that naturally pulls the ear back to the tonic C.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: In 'Paint Like a Beast', what did students mainly use to apply paint, besides brushes?
questions.why: Students used sponges and rags alongside brushes to build loose, textured marks — the activity avoided tools like rulers or fine-tip pens that produce neat, controlled lines.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these events in Japan's feudal land exchange by what happens, from first to last
questions.why: A lord first grants land to a vassal, the vassal accepts the duty owed in return, then provides military service, and the lord protects them in turn — this loyalty exchange held Japan's feudal system together.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these stages of a continuity-and-change enquiry by scale, from narrowest to widest
questions.why: A continuity-and-change enquiry builds outward: starting from one source detail, to an event, to a time period, and finally the whole era, so judgements rest on solid evidence rather than guesswork.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What does the Prologue reveal before the play even begins?
questions.why: The Prologue tells the audience straight away that these 'star-crossed lovers' will die, creating dramatic irony for everything that follows.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What is the genre of Romeo and Juliet?
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy — a play that ends in the deaths of its main characters, unlike a comedy (happy ending) or a history (based on real kings and events).
